## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

Verses from the *Aññāsikoṇḍaññattheragāthā* share extensive parallels across early Buddhist verse anthologies. SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels to verses in the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 277, 278, and 279), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 97–134, *Maguvagga*), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 358–375, *Māggavagga*), Chinese translations of the *Dharmapada* and *Udānavarga* traditions (T 210.28, T 212.13, and T 213.12), and the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* (UV 12, Uv Kg 12, and UVS 12) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently confirms this connection through automatic cross-language alignment with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga de Subaši* [DharmaNexus].
Within the Pali tradition, significant internal text reuse is documented. DharmaNexus identifies substantial shared passages between this poem and the commentaries (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), as well as parallel verses in the *Khadiravaniyarevatattheragāthā* (Thag 14.1, segments 13.1–16.3) and the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 277–280, matching segments 3.4–7.1) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, lines or concepts from the text are cited or referenced in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 16.4, *Adhigayhamanasikārakathā*), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4 and Ne 37), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2), the *Niddesa* treatises (Mnd 4, Cnd 6, Cnd 12, and Cnd 16), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3.136) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
